name: Marcus Pacuvius
credit: Marcus Pacuvius, woodcut from Hartmann Schedel's Liber Chronicarum (Nuremberg, 1493) — an imagined portrait, as no likeness from his own time survives · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Marcus Pacuvius was born about 220 BC at Brundisium in southern Italy, the son of a sister of the poet Ennius. He was a painter as well as a poet, and he settled in Rome, where he wrote tragedies on Greek mythological themes, among them Antiopa, Chryses, Hermiona, Iliona, Medus, Niptra, Periboea and Teucer, as well as a play on a Roman subject, Paulus. Cicero names him the finest of the Roman tragic poets.

Only fragments of his plays survive, as quotations in Cicero, Varro, Nonius, Gellius and other writers. Later in life he retired to Tarentum, where he is said to have died around 130 BC. Here his fragments are given as Garrod printed them in the Oxford Book of Latin Verse (1912), together with the epitaph he composed for himself, which Gellius preserved.

poems.title: Teucer (fragment): Fortunam insanam
poems.author: Marcus Pacuvius
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Latin Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Fortunam insanam esse et caecam et brutam perhibent philosophi,
saxoque instare in globoso praedicant uolubili:
id quo saxum impulerit fors, eo cadere Fortunam autumant.
insanam autem esse aiunt, quia atrox incerta instabilis siet:
caecam ob eam rem esse iterant, quia nil cernat quo sese adplicet:
brutam, quia dignum atque indignum nequeat internoscere.
sunt autem alii philosophi, qui contra Fortuna negant
ullam miseriam esse, temeritatem esse omnia autumant.
id magis ueri simile esse usus reapse experiundo edocet:
uelut Orestes modo fuit rex, factust mendicus modo.

poems.title: Teucer (fragment): Sic profectione laeti
poems.author: Marcus Pacuvius
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Latin Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Sic profectione laeti piscium lasciuiam
intuemur, nec tuendi satietas capier potest.
interea prope iam occidente sole inhorrescit mare,
tenebrae conduplicantur noctisque et nimbum obcaecat nigror,
flamma inter nubes coruscat, caelum tonitru contremit,
grando mixta imbri largifico subita praecipitans cadit,
undique omnes uenti erumpunt, saeui existunt turbines,
feruit aestu pelagus.

poems.title: Chryses (fragment): Hoc vide circum
poems.author: Marcus Pacuvius
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Latin Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Hoc uide circum supraque quod complexu continet terram
solisque exortu capessit candorem, occasu nigret,
id quod nostri caelum memorant, Grai perhibent aethera:
quidquid est hoc, omnia animat format alit auget creat
sepelit recipitque in sese omnia, omniumque idem est pater,
indidemque eadem aeque oriuntur de integro atque eodem occidunt.

poems.title: Hermiona (fragment): O flexanima
poems.author: Marcus Pacuvius
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Latin Verse (1912)
poems.text: O flexanima atque omnium regina rerum Oratio.

poems.title: Niptra (fragment): Conqueri fortunam
poems.author: Marcus Pacuvius
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Latin Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Conqueri fortunam aduersam, non lamentari decet:
id uiri est officium, fletus muliebri ingenio additus.

poems.title: Epitaph of Pacuvius
poems.author: Marcus Pacuvius
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Latin Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Adulescens tam etsi properas, hoc te saxulum
rogat ut se aspicias, deinde, quod scriptum est, legas.
hic sunt poetae Pacuui Marci sita
ossa. hoc uolebam, nescius ne esses. uale.
